title: personal-llm-experiment-mini-sheet-samir-2026-q1
content:
Mini experiment tracker (personal) - quick reference table and notes

Columns: date | model | prompt_id | quant | batch_size | seq_len | p50_ms | p95_ms | tokens_out | cost_est_per_1k_tokens | notes

2026-01-15 | redwood-ggml-v1 | prompt-012 | int8 | 1 | 256 | 22 | 48 | 320 | $0.45 | baseline local laptop run, stable output
2026-01-22 | redwood-ggml-v1 | prompt-012 | int8 | 4 | 256 | 90 | 210 | 1280 | $0.30 | batching improves throughput but p95 spikes on cold cache
2026-02-03 | redwood-ggml-v2 | prompt-013 | fp16 | 1 | 512 | 30 | 60 | 600 | $0.80 | higher quality, noticeably slower at 512
2026-02-14 | redwood-ggml-v2 | prompt-013 | int8 | 2 | 512 | 55 | 120 | 1200 | $0.40 | int8 reduces cost, small quality diff for this prompt
2026-02-25 | redwood-ggml-v2-qat | prompt-014 | qat8 | 1 | 256 | 20 | 45 | 280 | $0.35 | promising: QAT model kept quality while lowering latency
2026-02-28 | fallback-gpt-small | prompt-015 | fp16 | 1 | 128 | 12 | 24 | 150 | $0.50 | cheap fallback for high-load windows

Quick notes and hypotheses:
- Observed: Simple prompts (prompt-012) show good batching gains; long-sequence prompts still dominated by KV cache misses.
- Hypothesis: For seq_len > 400, fp16 model V2 with async KV prefetch reduces p95 by ~20%. Need to validate with 50-sample runs.
- Cost tradeoff: Int8 quantization reduces per-token cost ~2x vs fp16 but riskier for complex prompts (prompt-013).
- Batching policy: 4x batch looks good for throughput, but implement jitter/latency SLO guard to avoid p95 spike on bursty traffic.

Immediate next steps (personal TODO):
- [ ] Run 50-sample p95 validation for fp16 + KV prefetch on v2 (target by 2026-03-07)
- [ ] Add small script to collect cold vs warm cache p95 (capture 20 cold samples)
- [ ] Share preliminary table with Connor, ask for workload-matching prompts (EOD 2026-03-05)

Scratch: metric calc notes
- cost_est_per_1k_tokens = (instance_cost_per_min / tokens_per_min) * 1000 -> rough estimate, adjust later with real infra numbers
- tokens_out measured by local token counter script (tokenizer v2)

Linked tickets / ideas to create:
- PERF-llm-batching: test dynamic batching thresholds and jitter (create in JIRA)
- EVAL-quant-stability: small eval harness for QAT vs int8 on user prompts

Personal log: quick impressions after runs
- 2026-02-25 QAT run felt most promising — maintain quality, lower latency and cost; want to rerun with more prompts.
- Keep this file as a live mini-sheet; copy rows into /confluence/experiments when I have cleaned results.
